# Spawn power-ups in all combat gym scenes

## Headline

Add weighted-random, live-tunable power-up spawning (with random, enemy-avoiding placement and full collection) to the enemy-bearing combat gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`, backed by a new general game-rules config and the existing pluggable `PowerUpSpawner` interface.

## Original request (verbatim)

> We need to spawn power ups in all gym scenes. There should be a plugable spawner. The initial implementation will simply pick a power up at random from all those available and place it at a random place on the screen (not on top of enemies). The frequency of spawn will be a configuation in the main game config file (if no such file exists then create a config system).

## Problem statement

The enemy-bearing combat gyms — `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` — spawn no power-ups at all, so a tester cannot observe drop cadence, placement or collection while under real enemy pressure. The three power-up/weapon gyms that do spawn drops use a hard-coded round-robin sequence at fixed screen positions with a compile-time interval (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL`), which does not reflect the intended in-game weighted-random behaviour (GDD §4.4) and cannot be tuned live.

## Users

- **Players / playtesters** — want the combat gyms to demonstrate power-up drops during genuine enemy pressure, so collection and effect behaviour (shield, bomb, phase, teleport, extra life, magnet) can be observed in context.
- **Game developers** — want a pluggable spawner plus a live-tunable game-rules config so spawn frequency and drop weights can be adjusted without editing scene code, and so the gyms reuse one shared implementation instead of per-scene copies.

### Example user stories

- As a playtester, I want power-ups to drop in the enemy and boss gyms so I can observe collection and effects while dodging real threats.
- As a developer, I want a live-tunable spawn-frequency control in the combat gyms so I can dial in the drop cadence without rebuilding.
- As a developer, I want the spawn ID selection and the spawn placement to be separate pluggable strategies so different scenes or difficulty tiers can swap either independently.
- As a developer, I want drop weights to follow the GDD rarity guidance (Extra Life rarer than standard drops) by default.

## Scope

**In scope:** `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) and `GymBoss`.

**Out of scope (already spawn, or enemy-free):** `GymPowerUps`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPlayer`, `GymIndex`. Converting these to the new random spawner/placement is a candidate follow-up, not part of this item.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/spawner.ts` already provides the pluggable `PowerUpSpawner<T>` interface with `RoundRobinSpawner` and `WeightedRandomSpawner` (injectable RNG, runtime `setWeight`, equal initial weights) — the "pluggable spawner" seam already exists for ID selection.
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` provides the shared grow → hold → shrink → despawn lifecycle and collection gating.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` (`EffectsRegistry`) tracks all active effects; `src/ui/HUD.ts` renders them (with a `showLives` option).
- `src/core/config.ts` is a localStorage-backed config system for `ShipConfig`, but there is **no** general game-rules config; power-up timing lives as hard-coded constants in `src/core/constants.ts` (`POWER_UP_SPAWN_INTERVAL = 12.5`).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` is the shared base for `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`; it has a `Player`, enemy entities/bullets and a wipe→respawn lifecycle, but no power-up layer and no HUD/`EffectsRegistry`.
- `GymPowerUpsCombat` is the reference implementation for combat-coupled collection (round-robin spawner, `EffectsRegistry`, P4 bullet clear, P7 teleport).

## Desired change

1. **General game-rules config** — new `src/core/rules.ts`, localStorage-backed and live-editable, mirroring the `src/core/config.ts` pattern (defaults merge, corrupt-JSON fallback). It holds the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID drop weights for P3–P9, defaulting to the GDD §4.4 rarity guidance (standard ~15–20 %, P8 Extra Life ~5 %, expressed as relative weights).
2. **Pluggable placement strategy** — new `src/powerups/placement.ts` exposing a `PowerUpPlacement` interface plus a `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation that chooses a random on-screen position (inside a margin) that does **not** overlap a live enemy body or the player, retries up to a configurable attempt limit, and then falls back to a deterministic safe position.
3. **Wire into the shared base** — `GymFormationScene` (covering both `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss`) gains an optional power-up layer: a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights and an injectable RNG), the placement strategy, the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle, and drop tracking. One drop on screen at a time, next spawn on the configured interval.
4. **Full collection** — in both scenes, drops are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap) and apply their effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry`; the standalone HUD renders active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets (no enemy damage), P7 is usable via S/↓ (nearest-safe-spot teleport + P6 on arrival), P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks.
5. **Live spawn-interval control** — a DOM-overlay slider (patterned on `GymPlayer`) edits the spawn interval in the running combat gym and persists it through the rules config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** A new `src/core/rules.ts` exposes a general game-rules config containing the power-up spawn interval (default 12.5 s) and per-ID weights for P3–P9 (standard IDs equal, P8 Extra Life rarer, per GDD §4.4). Values load over defaults and persist via localStorage, with corrupt-JSON fallback. Unit tests cover defaults, round-trip, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- [ ] **AC2 (testing/validation):** A pluggable `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` implementation in `src/powerups/placement.ts` pick a random in-bounds position that does not overlap a live enemy body **or** the player, retry up to a configurable attempt limit, and return a deterministic safe fallback when no free position is found. Unit tests with an injected RNG verify non-overlap given supplied enemy/player positions, the retry path and the fallback path.
- [ ] **AC3:** `GymEnemies` (every archetype) and `GymBoss` spawn one power-up at a time on the configured interval, selecting the ID through a `PowerUpSpawner` (default `WeightedRandomSpawner` over P3–P9 with the rules weights) and positioning it through the placement strategy. Scene-level tests verify the spawn cadence and that spawned drops never overlap live enemies or the player.
- [ ] **AC4:** Spawned drops use the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and are fly-over collectible (≥ 3 % scale + hull overlap); collecting applies the effect through a shared `EffectsRegistry` in both scenes. Tests cover at least one collectible path per scene.
- [ ] **AC5:** Both combat gyms render the standalone HUD for active effects; P4 clears on-screen enemy bullets without damaging enemies, P7 teleport works via S/↓, P8 updates the lives counter and P9 stacks. Tests verify each effect is observable in a combat gym.
- [ ] **AC6:** A live spawn-interval control in the combat gyms changes the spawn cadence of the running scene and persists the value through the rules config; a test covers live application and persistence.
- [ ] **AC7:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies; reuse `PowerUpSpawner`, `PowerUp`, `EffectsRegistry`, `HUD`, `icons` and `audio` — do not fork existing implementations.
- Tests must be deterministic: inject the RNG used by the spawner and the placement strategy; never rely on the real render loop (drive scenes via `gameHarness`).
- The gym index and scene discovery must remain untouched — the shared base class carries the change to all archetypes.
- All written output in UK English.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "all combat gym scenes" means the enemy-bearing formation gyms `GymEnemies` and `GymBoss` only.
- **Assumption:** GDD §4.4 percentages are expressed as relative weights (for example standard = 4, P8 Extra Life = 1) rather than literal probabilities; the existing `WeightedRandomSpawner` semantics are reused unchanged.
- **Assumption:** "not on top of enemies" also excludes the player body, but proximity to the player is permitted (confirmed).
- **Assumption:** live edits apply immediately to the running scene; the next spawn uses the updated interval.
- **Risk:** adding an `EffectsRegistry`/HUD/drop layer to the shared `GymFormationScene` could regress existing `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss` behaviour — mitigate by wiring incrementally and running the full suite before review.
- **Risk (scope creep):** random placement + weighted spawning are also desirable in the three power-up/weapon gyms; this is recorded as a follow-up candidate rather than expanding this item.
- **Risk:** non-deterministic placement could make tests flaky — mitigate with injected, seeded RNGs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/rules.ts` — New general game-rules config (spawn interval + per-ID weights), localStorage-backed and live-editable.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — New unit tests for defaults, persistence, partial merge and corrupt fallback.
- `src/powerups/placement.ts` — New `PowerUpPlacement` interface and `RandomAvoidingPlacement` strategy.
- `src/powerups/placement.test.ts` — New unit tests for non-overlap, retry and fallback behaviour.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Wire the spawner, placement strategy, drop lifecycle, collection, `EffectsRegistry` and HUD into the shared combat base.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Extend with spawn-cadence, placement and collection tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Enable and configure the power-up layer per archetype.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Scene-level spawning/collection tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — Enable and configure the power-up layer.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts` — Scene-level spawning/collection tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Re-source or alias the power-up spawn-interval default from the new rules config.
- `README.md` — Document the combat gyms' power-up behaviour.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Note the configurable/pluggable spawning for the combat gyms.

## Related work

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTE8EB6Q007EU0J** – Icons: code-drawn icons for P3, P4, P6, P7 (completed) — the drop icons this work reuses.
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed) — the shared base scene/archetype coverage added here.
- **AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM** – Thrust flame invisible on player ship; should scale with thrustAcceleration (completed) — unrelated, surfaced by keyword overlap only.

Also directly relevant (from manual context gathering, not in the automated report):
- **AH-0MTCPL9NA0025ZUI** – In-Game spawning should not be round robin (completed) — introduced the pluggable `PowerUpSpawner` interface and `WeightedRandomSpawner` this work builds on.
- **AH-0MTCNZPHN003C5E1** – Power-up core lifecycle + tunable constants (completed) — the shared `PowerUp` lifecycle and constants.
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** – Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) (completed) — the reference implementation for combat collection, P4 bullet clear and P7 teleport.

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — GDD §4.4 (power-up rarity/drop rates) and §6.4 (gym scenes).
- `README.md` — gym scene documentation (adding a new gym scene / gym descriptions).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — enemy gym implementation notes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope):** Which scenes are "all combat gym scenes"? — **Answer (operator):** "a" — the enemy-bearing formation gyms only: `GymEnemies` (all archetypes) + `GymBoss`. The other three gyms already demonstrate spawning. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (pool/randomness):** Which power-ups are in the random pool and with what probabilities? — **Answer (operator):** "b" — all 7 catalogue IDs (P3–P9), weighted per GDD (standard ~15–20 %, P8 Extra Life ~5 %) via `WeightedRandomSpawner`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (config):** Where should the spawn-frequency config live? — **Answer (operator):** "c (live editable)" — a general new game-rules config (e.g. `src/core/rules.ts`) that power-up settings join, live-editable (localStorage + gym controls). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q4 (collection):** Should drops be collectible with effects applied, or spawn-only? — **Answer (operator):** "b" — full collection with effects + HUD in `GymEnemies`/`GymBoss`. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q5 (placement):** Placement constraints? — **Answer (operator):** "a + avoid spawning on player (near player is OK)" — reject only on overlap with a live enemy body or the player; retry to a limit, then deterministic fallback. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q6 (live-edit surface):** What should the gym control panel expose? — **Answer (operator):** "a" — spawn interval only. Source: interactive reply.


## Appendix: Plan session (Q7)

- **Q7 (plan approval):** Presented the 8-feature decomposition — F1 verification matrix & test fixtures, F2 game-rules config, F3 avoiding placement strategy, F4 base-scene spawning cadence, F5 collection + effects + HUD, F6 live spawn-interval control, F7 documentation, F8 full-suite verification & AC audit — with default weights (standard IDs = 4, P8 Extra Life = 1) and spawn interval = 12.5 s, plus dependency edges and test-first ordering. — **Answer (operator):** "LGTM" — the plan, ordering, dependencies and defaults are approved as presented. Source: interactive reply. Final: approved.
- Q1–Q6 were captured during intake and remain in effect (see Appendix above); no answers were changed or superseded.

## Plan: child work items

| Feature | Work item | Covers parent AC |
|---|---|---|
| F1 Verification matrix and test fixtures | AH-0MU44M8EI000CPB0 | AC8 (verification), test-first enabler |
| F2 Game-rules config with tests | AH-0MU44M8PJ008LI66 | AC1 |
| F3 Pluggable avoiding placement strategy | AH-0MU44M90T003EQ2G | AC2 |
| F4 Spawn power-ups in combat base | AH-0MU44M9CA007GBTZ | AC3 |
| F5 Collect drops with effects and HUD | AH-0MU44M9NQ0006613 | AC4, AC5 |
| F6 Live spawn-interval control | AH-0MU44M9Z0007ZGPI | AC6 |
| F7 Documentation for combat spawning | AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD | AC7 |
| F8 Full-suite verification and AC audit | AH-0MU44MALL0006THI | AC8 |

Dependency edges: F2←F1, F3←F1, F4←F2, F4←F3, F5←F4, F6←F2, F6←F4, F7←F5, F7←F6, F8←F5, F8←F6, F8←F7.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-16 13:27 UTC — plan skill decomposed this item into 8 children (F1–F8) with dependency edges; test-first ordering enforced (F1 verification/fixtures blocks F2/F3); defaults recorded (standard weights = 4, P8 = 1; spawn interval 12.5 s) per GDD §4.4; child descriptions augmented with explicit parent-AC coverage references to satisfy the AC-coverage review (100 % coverage, recommendation `proceed`); stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Respawn player in same spot

## Original request (verbatim seed)

> When a player is hit show they should respawn in the same spot. The routine should be: 1) Play SFX
> 2) Play VFX (expand the ship by 50% then contract to normal size) 3) respawn ship in current
> location and orientation (with existing invincibility time out)

## Problem statement

When the player ship is hit in a gym scene it is currently **relocated to a fixed spawn point**
(centre screen) rather than staying where it was hit. The operator wants a hit to read as a short
"damage beat" at the point of impact: play the existing SFX, play a scale VFX (ship grows to 150%
then shrinks back to 100%) **in addition to** the existing particle burst, then leave the ship
**stopped dead at the same position and orientation** it had when hit, under the existing post-hit
invulnerability window.

Initial spawn is **not** changing: a new game / scene start still spawns the ship centre screen.

## Users

- **Players** — a hit should look and feel like a damage flash on the ship they are flying, not a
  teleport back to the middle of the screen that loses their position in the level.
- **Designers / AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need one unambiguous, testable rule for
  "respawn in place" so all player-bearing scenes behave identically.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my ship to stay where it was hit so I keep my position and the hit reads
  as a damage effect rather than a relocation.
- As a **player**, I want a clear visual beat (ship pulses to 150% and back to normal) layered on the
  existing explosion so the hit is unmistakable, plus the existing hit sound.
- As a **developer**, I want the in-place respawn implemented once in the shared player-hit path so
  every gym scene inherits identical behaviour and tests stay cheap.
- As a **developer**, I want the start-of-scene spawn position to remain unchanged, so this change
  cannot silently regress "player spawns centre screen".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — In-place respawn after death:** After a player hit, the ship occupies the **same (x, y)**
  it had at the moment of the hit; it is not relocated to the scene's fixed spawn point
  (`playerSpawnX/Y`, `PLAYER_SPAWN`, or centre screen).
- [ ] **AC2 — Spawn (new game / scene start) unchanged:** The initial spawn position is **not** changed
  — the ship still spawns centre screen (`PLAYER_SPAWN` / scene config) on scene start. Only the
  post-hit respawn is in-place.
- [ ] **AC3 — State on respawn:** The ship's **facing/orientation at the moment of the hit is
  preserved** (the respawn must not reset rotation to 0 / facing to a default) and its
  **velocity/momentum is reset to zero** — the ship is **stopped dead** at the hit spot.
- [ ] **AC4 — Hit VFX (scale pulse):** The hit plays a visible scale VFX on the ship: scale **expands
  to ~150%** of normal and then **contracts back to 100%**, ending at exactly 1.0 scale. The VFX is
  observable from tests (or deterministically assertable) without pixel comparison.
- [ ] **AC5 — Hit VFX is additive:** The scale pulse plays **in addition to** the existing
  particle-explosion burst (`_spawnPlayerExplosion` / shared particle helper). Entity death VFX is
  unchanged.
- [ ] **AC6 — Hit SFX and invulnerability unchanged:** The existing hit/destruction SFX still plays
  exactly once per hit (no double-play, no new audio asset), and the post-hit invulnerability window
  and blink keep their existing per-scene values (`PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE` = 1.5 s in
  `GymFormationScene`; `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION` = 0.8 s in `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC7 — Scope consistent:** The in-place respawn + scale VFX applies to **every player-hit path**
  — `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (inherited by `GymEnemies`, `GymBoss`, and the formation gyms) and
  `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` — so no scene keeps the old relocate-to-spawn behaviour.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** Unit/scene tests cover: (a) post-hit position equals pre-hit
  position; (b) pre-hit facing is preserved exactly (a silent reset-to-0 must fail); (c) velocity is
  zero after the hit; (d) the scale pulse runs 1.0 → 1.5 → 1.0; (e) the particle burst still spawns
  (additive VFX); (f) SFX fires once; (g) invulnerability is set and a second hit is ignored while it
  is active; (h) initial spawn position is unchanged. All tests pass.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.2 ("Collisions &
  respawn") is updated from "the ship respawns at its spawn position" to the in-place rule, noting
  that the *respawn* clause of AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC4 is superseded while its *initial spawn* rule
  stands. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
  README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Test suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Initial spawn must not change** — centre-screen spawn (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC1–AC3) remains in
  force; only the post-hit respawn rule is superseded.
- **No new audio asset** — reuse the existing destruction SFX (`playDestructionSound`).
- **No change to lives/score model** — the player is never destroyed (infinite lives in gyms); only
  the respawn location/orientation/velocity and the hit VFX change.
- **No change to the collision radii or hit conditions** that trigger `_hitPlayer()`.
- **Deterministic tests preferred** — Phaser tweens are awkward to assert; expose an observable seam
  (e.g. a tracked scale-VFX handle or a `getPlayerHitVfx()` accessor) rather than relying on
  wall-clock tween completion.
- **Merge-order awareness** — `GymFormationScene.ts` is a shared core library touched by many gym
  items; keep the diff surgical.

## Existing state

- `GymFormationScene._hitPlayer()` (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, ~line 834):
  increments `playerHitCount`, calls `playDestructionSound()`, calls
  `_spawnPlayerExplosion(player.x, player.y)` (particle burst, `SHIP_COLOR`/`SHIP_SIZE`), then
  `this.player.respawn(this.playerSpawnX, this.playerSpawnY)` and sets
  `playerInvulnerable = PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE` (1.5 s) with blink reset.
- `playerSpawnX/Y` are captured at `create()` from `config.player.x/y` (centre screen,
  `PLAYER_SPAWN = { x: 480, y: 270 }` per AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT).
- `Player.respawn(x, y)` (`src/entities/Player.ts`, ~line 800) **hard-resets** the movement state to
  `{ x, y, vx: 0, vy: 0, facing: 0 }`, calls `setRotation(0)`, zeroes thruster flames and stops the
  thruster hum — i.e. it zeroes velocity (which we want) but **also discards orientation** (which we
  must preserve).
- `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, ~line 657) independently
  hard-codes a relocate to `GAME_WIDTH/2, GAME_HEIGHT/2`, zeroes velocity, plays
  `playDestructionSound()`, and starts invulnerability = `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION` (0.8 s).
  It has **no** particle or scale VFX.
- Particle burst VFX for player death was introduced by "Wire particle VFX to death paths"
  (AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J) as the **primary** death VFX for both entities and the player; it stays.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7.2 ("Collisions & respawn", ~lines 406–417) documents
  the current relocate-to-spawn behaviour; ~line 416 states "the ship respawns at its spawn
  position".
- Superseded in part: "Player should spawn center screen" (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT) AC4 required "the
  respawn position matches the initial spawn position (center screen)" — its respawn clause is
  superseded by this item; its initial-spawn clauses remain valid.

## Desired change

On a player hit, run exactly this sequence at the ship's current position:

1. **SFX** — play the existing destruction sound once.
2. **VFX** — scale the ship up to ~150% and back down to 100% (a single expand/contract pulse),
   **in addition to** the existing particle-explosion burst.
3. **Respawn** — leave the ship at its **current location and current orientation**, with
   **velocity zeroed (stopped dead)**, and start the **existing** post-hit invulnerability window
   (blink).

No relocation to the fixed spawn point, and no orientation reset. The initial spawn position on
scene start is unchanged.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` becomes in-place; add the scale-VFX
  pulse (and an observable seam); keep SFX, particle burst and `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE`.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `respawn()` needs a variant/mode that preserves orientation (currently
  forces `facing: 0` / `setRotation(0)`); velocity-zeroing behaviour is retained or a new
  `respawnInPlace()` is added.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — `_hitPlayer()` must adopt the same in-place + scale VFX +
  SFX behaviour (currently hard-codes centre-screen relocation and has no VFX).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — possibly a `PLAYER_HIT_SCALE_PEAK` (1.5) / pulse-duration constant.
  `PLAYER_SPAWN` must remain `{ x: 480, y: 270 }`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts`,
  `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — update/extend tests for position, orientation, velocity, scale
  pulse, particle burst, SFX, invulnerability and unchanged initial spawn.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §7.2 collisions/respawn wording.

## Related work

- **Player should spawn center screen (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT)** — **partially superseded**: its AC4
  respawn clause ("respawn position matches the initial spawn position") is replaced by the in-place
  rule; its AC1–AC3 initial-spawn rule (centre screen on scene start) remains in force and is
  guarded by AC2 here.
- **Wire particle VFX to death paths (AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J)** — introduced the particle burst as the
  *primary* player-death VFX (`_spawnPlayerExplosion`). Operator decision: the new scale pulse is
  **additive** to it (AC5).
- **Implement: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (AH-0MTECNG8W00403EH)** —
  created the original hit → SFX + explosion + respawn-at-spawn + invulnerability path.
- **Test: Core scene — collision detection and player hit/respawn (AH-0MTECNG4K0071TIB)** — existing
  hit/respawn test coverage that will need updating.
- **If player crashes into an enemy, they both die (AH-0MTV7JOLU006W8PT)** — the entity-collision
  branch also calls `_hitPlayer()`; it inherits the in-place rule decided here.
- **Implement/Test: Wipe detection, 3s countdown, and respawn in GymFormationScene
  (AH-0MTHCD0BQ000JFZ4 / AH-0MTHCFDAD009B3JG)** — the *formation* respawn lifecycle (unrelated
  mechanism, same file and same `respawn` vocabulary — do not conflate).
- **Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library (AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3)** — why the player-hit
  logic lives in one shared base class.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Resolved — reversing a producer-approved AC (partial):** AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT AC4 is superseded
  **for respawn only**, by explicit operator decision (Appendix Q1). Its initial-spawn rule stands;
  AC2 is the regression guard. Note the supersede in the §7.2 documentation update (AC9).
- **Resolved — VFX relationship:** the scale pulse plays **in addition to** the particle burst
  (Appendix Q3); entity death VFX unchanged.
- **Resolved — velocity:** zeroed on respawn — "stopped dead" (Appendix Q2).
- **Risk — orientation is not currently recoverable after `respawn()`:** `Player.respawn()` discards
  `facing`; the implementer must capture position/orientation **before** calling any reset, or add an
  in-place variant. Tests must assert the exact pre-hit facing (not merely "unchanged"), so a silent
  reset-to-0 cannot pass (AC8b).
- **Risk — two independent hit paths:** `GymPowerUpsCombat._hitPlayer()` does not extend
  `GymFormationScene` and currently has neither particle nor scale VFX; it must be brought in line
  or the scope AC (AC7) fails. Consider extracting the hit beat into a shared helper to avoid a third
  divergence.
- **Risk — tween test flakiness:** scale tweens are time-based; expose a deterministic seam (AC4) or
  drive the pulse from `tick(dt)` as the countdown is, to keep the suite stable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** keep the change to the hit/respawn beat only. Extra ideas surfaced while
  planning (e.g. brief slow-motion on hit, hit-screen shake, per-scene VFX variation, hit-count UI)
  must be recorded as **linked new work items**, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** "expand the ship by 50%" means peak scale 1.5× of the ship's normal scale, returning
  to exactly 1.0.
- **Assumption:** `GymPlayer` has no hit logic, so it is out of scope unless the operator says
  otherwise.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Respawn in place **supersedes** AC4 of *Player should spawn center screen*
  (AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT), which required respawn to relocate to the centre-screen spawn point. Should
  the in-place rule replace the relocate-to-spawn rule in **all** player-hit scenes
  (GymFormationScene base → GymEnemies / GymBoss / formation gyms, plus GymPowerUpsCombat)?
  [Proposed: yes — respawn in place everywhere, old AC4 superseded.]" — **Answer (operator): "When
  starting a new game, spawn central. When re-spawning after death supersede."** Source: interactive
  reply. Interpretation (accepted): the **initial spawn stays centre screen**; the **respawn**
  behaviour is superseded to in-place across all player-hit scenes. Final: AC1 (in-place respawn) +
  AC2 (initial spawn unchanged) + AC7 (all hit paths).
- Q2: "At the moment of a hit, should the ship **keep its pre-hit velocity/momentum** (so it carries
  on drifting after the VFX), or be **stopped dead** at the hit spot while preserving position and
  facing? [Proposed: stopped dead — position + orientation preserved, velocity zeroed, matching the
  existing `respawn()` behaviour for velocity.]" — **Answer (operator): "stop dead"**. Source:
  interactive reply. Final: AC3 — orientation preserved, velocity zeroed.
- Q3: "Does the expand-to-150%-then-contract scale VFX **replace** the existing particle-explosion
  burst on player hit (`_spawnPlayerExplosion`, added as the *primary* death VFX by
  AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J), or **play in addition to** it? [Proposed: replace for the player hit (one
  clear damage beat); keep entities' particle bursts unchanged.]" — **Answer (operator): "in
  addition"**. Source: interactive reply. Final: AC5 — scale pulse is additive to the particle
  burst; entity death VFX unchanged.
- Research note: the player-hit path was read directly at `GymFormationScene.ts:697–843`,
  `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts:657–675` and `Player.ts:800`. The centre-screen spawn rule and its AC4
  wording were read from AH-0MTVYBCUW008BEQT; the particle-burst-as-primary-VFX decision from
  AH-0MTVID8RQ002DJ0J AC1–AC3. Invulnerability constants: `PLAYER_RESPAWN_INVULNERABLE = 1.5` and
  `COMBAT_HIT_INVULNERABLE_DURATION = 0.8` in `src/core/constants.ts`.

# Documentation for combat spawning

## Goal

As a developer, I want the repository documentation to describe the new configurable, weighted, pluggable power-up spawning in the combat gyms so future work has an accurate reference.

## Scope

Documentation and code comments only — no behaviour changes.

## Deliverables

- `./README.md` — document the combat gyms' power-up behaviour (weighted random ID selection, avoiding random placement, live spawn-interval control, collection + effects).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — note the configurable/pluggable spawning for the combat gyms (§4.4 power-ups, §6.4 gym scenes), including the relative-weight interpretation of the GDD rarity guidance.
- JSDoc/code comments on `src/core/rules.ts` and `src/powerups/placement.ts`.
- Remove or update stale references to the hard-coded spawn interval.

**Key Files:**

- `./README.md`
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`
- `src/core/rules.ts`
- `src/powerups/placement.ts`

**Acceptance Criteria below.**

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: `README.md` documents the combat gym power-up behaviour and the rules config.

- [ ] AC3: `src/core/rules.ts` and `src/powerups/placement.ts` carry accurate JSDoc describing their behaviour.
- [ ] AC4: No stale references remain to a compile-time-only power-up spawn interval for the combat gyms.
